stances.reasoning: Jehlen did not cosponsor the Abortion Access Act per Act on Mass legislator tracking, which would have guaranteed abortion at all stages with public funding. Her general progressive record and reproductive rights support places her as supporting abortion access through the first trimester and in cases of rape, incest, or health risk, without the all-stages publicly-funded approach.

Co-sponsored the Stop Corporate Offshoring bill and authored a Commonwealth Beacon op-ed arguing Massachusetts should solve budget challenges by closing corporate loopholes and tax dodges. Also sponsored S.2017 (a digital advertising tax on large corporations), consistent with banning private corporate money from politics and publicly funding campaigns.

Co-sponsored the Campaign Childcare bill per Act on Mass tracking, and sponsored S.2019 to support childcare providers through the tax code, reflecting a commitment to significantly expanding subsidies and public investment in early education beyond current levels.

Sponsored the RAISE Act (S.380) to address racial disparities in school suspensions and expulsions, co-sponsored Environmental Justice legislation, and was elected in 2005 with support from SEIU and progressive civil rights organizations. Her legislative record consistently addresses systemic discrimination through new accountability measures.

Co-sponsored 100% Renewable Energy by 2045 and Environmental Justice legislation per Act on Mass tracking. Sponsored S.2292 requiring new buildings to be fossil-fuel-free and S.1548 to reduce transportation pollution in overburdened communities, reflecting a rapid transition rather than an immediate full ban on all carbon activities.

Co-sponsored the Safe Communities Act, which limits state/local law enforcement cooperation with ICE, prohibits police from asking about immigration status, and would allow deportation only in cases of serious criminal convictions, not for all undocumented residents regardless of history.

Co-sponsored Stop Corporate Offshoring and authored a Commonwealth Beacon op-ed questioning whether Massachusetts tax cuts for wealthy corporations are necessary for competitiveness, advocating instead for public services investment. Her profile focuses on worker protections and small-business support over large corporate subsidies.

Sponsored S.2291 protecting ratepayers from gas pipeline expansion costs and S.2292 requiring fossil-fuel-free new construction. Her co-sponsorship of the 100% Renewable by 2045 bill signals stopping new fossil fuel expansion without an immediate complete extraction ban.

Opposed Tufts University's proposed 700-student dormitory project at 401 Boston Avenue in 2025, favoring growth only where existing infrastructure and community character support it. Her tenant-protective housing bills prioritize stability over maximizing new development permits.

Co-sponsored Medicare for All per Act on Mass legislator tracking (H.1239/S.744, the Massachusetts single-payer bill providing universal coverage with no premiums or copays funded through a payroll tax). This is the strongest possible pro-single-payer stance at the state level.

Co-sponsored the Prison Moratorium and Age of Criminal Majority to 21, signaling a decriminalization-oriented approach. Sponsored medical parole access (S.2857) and substance use reform in corrections (S.1706), consistent with redirecting enforcement budgets toward services over criminalization of survival behaviors.

Co-sponsorship of Prison Moratorium and criminal justice reform bills (medical parole, substance-use commission) reflects a shelter-and-services-first rather than enforcement-first orientation toward public space and homelessness.

Sponsored S.22 (Somerville rent regulation), S.1447 (statewide rent stabilization), S.998 (tenant first right of refusal), and co-sponsored Lift the Ban on Local Tenant Protections, plus S.475 (housing stability for older adults) and S.870 (home care rate-setting), reflecting strong public investment in housing affordability through rent caps and tenant protections.

Co-sponsored the Safe Communities Act, which maintains legal immigration pathways while protecting undocumented long-term residents from enforcement based on status alone, reflecting a keep-legal-immigration-open policy with services protections regardless of immigration status.

Co-sponsored the Prison Moratorium (5-year pause on new jail/prison construction) per Act on Mass tracking, and sponsored S.1707 (medical parole access), S.1706 (substance use commission in corrections), S.1134 (probation violations reform), and S.84 (cannabis career pathways for justice-involved individuals), redirecting resources away from incarceration.

Sponsored S.1132 (wrongful conviction victim compensation) and S.1136 (preventing false confessions), both lowering barriers to justice for those wrongfully harmed by the legal system. Her entire criminal justice portfolio favors easy court access and remedies for wrongful state action.

Co-sponsored Age of Criminal Majority to 21 and Prison Moratorium; her criminal justice bills consistently favor diversion over detention and signal skepticism toward prosecutorial over-reach and high pretrial detention.

Co-sponsored Age of Criminal Majority to 21 (diverting young adults from adult prison) and the Prison Moratorium, and sponsored medical parole (S.1707) and substance use reform in corrections (S.1706). Her entire criminal justice focus centers on rehabilitation and reducing incarceration rather than punishment.

Sponsored S.1136 (preventing false confessions) to create accountability for coercive interrogation practices, and co-sponsored the Safe Communities Act to limit police cooperation with ICE. Favors settling valid accountability claims through reform legislation.

Did not co-sponsor Life Without Parole per Act on Mass; her entire criminal justice record supports diversion, medical parole, and age-of-majority reforms. Consistently favors diversion programs when available over maximum incarceration.

Did not co-sponsor Open Meeting Law reform or Public Records Law reforms per Act on Mass tracking, and has not signed the Act on Mass transparency pledge. She has not prioritized expanding public records access, placing her at a balance rather than default-to-open stance.

Co-sponsored the Safe Communities Act (H.2288/S.1510), which would prohibit local police from asking about immigration status, refuse ICE detainers unless court-ordered, and bar city employees from sharing immigration information with federal agencies.

Sponsored S.1548 (transportation pollution air quality for overburdened communities), S.607 (invasive species response), S.608 (combined sewer overflows), and co-sponsored Environmental Justice legislation, reflecting strict environmental protection with full offset requirements for development impacts.

Co-sponsored Medicare for All on Act on Mass (H.1239/S.744, the Massachusetts single-payer bill covering all residents). Chairs the Joint Committee on Aging and Independence and sponsored S.476 (long-term services benefit program) and S.870 (home care rate-setting) to expand public coverage for seniors.

Co-sponsored Prison Moratorium and Age of Criminal Majority to 21 but has not advocated for defunding police departments. Her approach maintains current staffing while shifting non-violent and behavioral health calls to alternative responses, consistent with her medical parole and substance-use-in-corrections bills.

Long-serving progressive Democrat who endorsed Bernie Sanders and aligns with Act on Mass progressive agenda. Her democratic reform orientation consistently favors independent oversight, aligning with independent commission with equal party representation rather than purely legislative control.

No specific religious freedom bills were found in her record. She strongly supports LGBTQ+ rights through the Healthy Youth Act and S.2155 (transgender commission), but no evidence of an explicit position on religious exemptions versus anti-discrimination law was found.

Sponsored S.22 (Somerville rent regulation authority), S.1447 (statewide rent stabilization enabling all cities and towns), and S.998 (tenant first right of refusal), plus co-sponsored Lift the Ban on Local Tenant Protections — supporting expanding rent control to all units with strong just-cause eviction protections.

Opposed Tufts University's proposed 700-student dormitory at 401 Boston Avenue in 2025, reflecting a neighborhood character protection stance consistent with requiring community input before major rezoning. Her legislative focus is on tenant stability rather than upzoning or streamlining development permits.

Co-sponsored the Healthy Youth Act (LGBTQ+ inclusive sex education) and S.2155 (transgender permanent commission), consistently advocating for full federal recognition and benefits.

Co-sponsored the Cherish Act (fully funded public higher education) per Act on Mass tracking and sponsored S.378 requiring transparency about charter school costs to public school budgets, reflecting opposition to diverting public funds to private or charter institutions.

Co-sponsored Stop Corporate Offshoring, sponsored S.2017 (digital advertising tax on large corporations), authored a Commonwealth Beacon op-ed arguing Massachusetts should close corporate loopholes and tax dodges, and serves as Vice-Chair of the Joint Committee on Revenue, consistently supporting significant tax increases on wealthy individuals and corporations.

Sponsored S.2155 to establish a permanent commission on transgender people, co-sponsored the Healthy Youth Act (LGBTQ+ inclusive education), and was elected in 2005 with MassEquality support. Her record strongly supports transgender people competing in accordance with their gender identity without restrictions.

Sponsored S.2397 (An Act relative to fare free buses), directly prioritizing public transit investment and access over road-focused spending, aligning with pedestrian/cycling/transit-first transportation policy.

Did not co-sponsor Voting Rights Restoration (restoring voting rights for people with felony convictions) per Act on Mass tracking. While she supports general voting access, her failure to support the most expansive voting rights bill places her at a standardize-voter-access position rather than automatic registration or full restoration.
